# The evidence catalog (A20)

<!-- Generated by `python -m eepy.explanations.catalog --write` from eepy/explanations/catalog.py. Do not edit by hand: change the catalog and regenerate. -->

Every reason EEPY can give for a nudge is one of these **evidence types**. Each type groups the
features that measure the same thing, so an explanation never says the same thing twice.
How the reasons are chosen: [A20_EXPLANATIONS.md](A20_EXPLANATIONS.md).

## Writing explanation lines (task C6)

EEPY says the explanation as one extra sentence right after the nudge's own line, in the same
tone (hedged when unsure, direct when sure), about the **top** evidence type of that decision.
To write your own sentences for a type, add a line to `behaviors/lines.yaml` called
`explain_<type>` (for example `explain_eye_closure`), with `hedged` and `direct` variants like
any other line. A wording is only used when all its placeholders have a value, so mix wordings
with and without numbers. Until a type has its own line, EEPY uses the default sentences below.
Only the placeholders of that type are allowed in its line (the validator checks).

```yaml
  explain_eye_closure:
    description: Said after a nudge when closing eyes were the main reason.
    variants:
      hedged:
        - "Your eyes seem to be closing a lot."
        - "It looks like your eyes were closed {closed_pct}% of the last minute."
      direct:
        - "Your eyes were closed {closed_pct}% of the last minute."
```

Values come from the last minute of measurements (the windows the model uses), and
`{minutes}` is how long the evidence built up for this decision. Only blink length is
measured against the person's own normal (`{times_normal}`); the other values are absolute.

| Type | Usually points to | Placeholders |
|---|---|---|
| [`eye_closure`](#eye_closure) | drowsy | `{closed_pct}`, `{times_normal}`, `{long_blinks}`, `{long_blinks_text}`, `{longest_s}`, `{closed_now_s}`, `{minutes}` |
| [`yawning`](#yawning) | drowsy | `{yawns}`, `{yawns_times}`, `{jaw_pct}`, `{minutes}` |
| [`nodding`](#nodding) | drowsy | `{nods}`, `{nods_times}`, `{minutes}` |
| [`looking_away`](#looking_away) | distracted | `{away_pct}`, `{away_seconds}`, `{away_for}`, `{away_count}`, `{away_times}`, `{on_work_pct}`, `{minutes}` |

## eye_closure

**Eyes closing.** The eyes are closed more, or for longer, than when alert: the share of time closed (PERCLOS), long or slow blinks, one very long closure (a microsleep), the eyes shut right now, and the eyes-closed action unit (AU43). They all measure the same closing eyes, so they count as one reason.

- **Usually points to:** drowsy
- **HMM features:** `perclos`, `blink_duration`, `long_blinks`, `microsleep`, `eyes_closed_now`, `au_eyes_closed`
- **Feature inputs:** `perclos_60s`, `blink_mean_ms_rel_60s`, `blink_mean_ms_60s`, `long_blinks_60s`, `blink_max_ms_60s`, `eyes_closed_now_s`, `AU43_active_60s`
- **In a contrast:** "your eyes were closing more" (for the decided state) / "your eyes stayed open" (against the runner-up)
- **Your line:** `explain_eye_closure` in behaviors/lines.yaml

| Placeholder | Unit | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{closed_pct}` | % | share of the last minute the eyes were closed | 34 |
| `{times_normal}` | x | blinks this many times as long as the person's own normal (only when calibrated, and at least 1.2) | 1.8 |
| `{long_blinks}` | count | long blinks in the last minute | 4 |
| `{long_blinks_text}` | words | "one long blink", "4 long blinks" | 4 long blinks |
| `{longest_s}` | seconds | the longest single closure in the last minute (only from 1 s) | 1.6 |
| `{closed_now_s}` | seconds | how long the eyes have been shut right now (only from 1 s) | 2.0 |
| `{minutes}` | minutes | how long the evidence has been building up for this decision (at least 1) | 3 |

Default sentences (the first one that can be filled is used; sentences that suit the feature that moved the belief most come first):

- *hedged:* "It looks like your eyes were closed about {closed_pct}% of the last minute." → "It looks like your eyes were closed about 34% of the last minute."
- *hedged:* "Your blinks seem about {times_normal} times longer than usual." → "Your blinks seem about 1.8 times longer than usual."
- *hedged:* "I noticed {long_blinks_text} in the last minute." → "I noticed 4 long blinks in the last minute."
- *hedged:* "Your eyes seemed to stay shut for {longest_s} seconds at one point." → "Your eyes seemed to stay shut for 1.6 seconds at one point."
- *hedged:* "Your eyes seem to be closing a lot."
- *direct:* "Your eyes were closed {closed_pct}% of the last minute." → "Your eyes were closed 34% of the last minute."
- *direct:* "Your blinks are {times_normal} times longer than your normal." → "Your blinks are 1.8 times longer than your normal."
- *direct:* "That was {long_blinks_text} in the last minute." → "That was 4 long blinks in the last minute."
- *direct:* "Your eyes stayed shut for {longest_s} seconds." → "Your eyes stayed shut for 1.6 seconds."
- *direct:* "Your eyes keep closing."

## yawning

**Yawning.** Yawns, and the jaw-drop action unit (AU26) that a yawn mostly is: one reason.

- **Usually points to:** drowsy
- **HMM features:** `yawns`, `au_jaw_drop`
- **Feature inputs:** `yawns_60s`, `AU26_active_60s`
- **In a contrast:** "you yawned" (for the decided state) / "you didn't yawn" (against the runner-up)
- **Your line:** `explain_yawning` in behaviors/lines.yaml

| Placeholder | Unit | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{yawns}` | count | yawns in the last minute | 2 |
| `{yawns_times}` | words | "once", "twice", "3 times" | twice |
| `{jaw_pct}` | % | share of the last minute the jaw-drop action unit was active | 12 |
| `{minutes}` | minutes | how long the evidence has been building up for this decision (at least 1) | 3 |

Default sentences (the first one that can be filled is used; sentences that suit the feature that moved the belief most come first):

- *hedged:* "I think I saw you yawn {yawns_times} in the last minute." → "I think I saw you yawn twice in the last minute."
- *hedged:* "You seem to be yawning."
- *direct:* "You've yawned {yawns_times} in the last minute." → "You've yawned twice in the last minute."
- *direct:* "You're yawning."

## nodding

**Nodding off.** The head dropping forward and jerking back up: nodding off.

- **Usually points to:** drowsy
- **HMM features:** `nods`
- **Feature inputs:** `nods_60s`
- **In a contrast:** "your head was dropping" (for the decided state) / "your head stayed up" (against the runner-up)
- **Your line:** `explain_nodding` in behaviors/lines.yaml

| Placeholder | Unit | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{nods}` | count | nods in the last minute | 1 |
| `{nods_times}` | words | "once", "twice", "3 times" | once |
| `{minutes}` | minutes | how long the evidence has been building up for this decision (at least 1) | 3 |

Default sentences (the first one that can be filled is used; sentences that suit the feature that moved the belief most come first):

- *hedged:* "It looked like your head dropped {nods_times} just now." → "It looked like your head dropped once just now."
- *hedged:* "Your head seems to be dropping."
- *direct:* "Your head dropped {nods_times} in the last minute." → "Your head dropped once in the last minute."
- *direct:* "You're nodding off."

## looking_away

**Looking away from the work.** The gaze is off the screen and the notes: the share of the last minute, and how long right now. Looking at a phone in the lap shows up here too (EEPY has no phone detector). When the gaze stays ON the work, the same evidence speaks against distraction.

- **Usually points to:** distracted
- **HMM features:** `gaze_off`, `away_now`
- **Feature inputs:** `gaze_off_ratio_60s`, `away_current_s`, `away_episodes_60s`
- **In a contrast:** "you were looking away from your work" (for the decided state) / "you kept looking at your work" (against the runner-up)
- **Your line:** `explain_looking_away` in behaviors/lines.yaml

| Placeholder | Unit | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{away_pct}` | % | share of the last minute looking away from the work | 45 |
| `{away_seconds}` | seconds | how long they have been looking away right now (from 10 s; shorter, the minute's share says more) | 12 |
| `{away_for}` | words | the same in words: "12 seconds", "about 2 minutes" | 12 seconds |
| `{away_count}` | count | how many separate times they looked away in the last minute (background detail: the model does not weigh the count itself; from 2) | 4 |
| `{away_times}` | words | "twice", "4 times" (from 2) | 4 times |
| `{on_work_pct}` | % | share of the last minute looking at the work | 55 |
| `{minutes}` | minutes | how long the evidence has been building up for this decision (at least 1) | 3 |

Default sentences (the first one that can be filled is used; sentences that suit the feature that moved the belief most come first):

- *hedged:* "You seem to have been looking away for {away_for}." → "You seem to have been looking away for 12 seconds."
- *hedged:* "It looks like you were looking away about {away_pct}% of the last minute." → "It looks like you were looking away about 45% of the last minute."
- *hedged:* "Your eyes seem to be off your work a lot."
- *direct:* "You've been looking away for {away_for}." → "You've been looking away for 12 seconds."
- *direct:* "You were looking away {away_pct}% of the last minute." → "You were looking away 45% of the last minute."
- *direct:* "You keep looking away from your work."

## Not in the catalog

- **Phone use.** EEPY has no phone detector; looking at a phone shows up as `looking_away`.
- **Time and model limits** (`dynamics` in the logged Explanation): how much of the belief's change came from the model's own drift over time and its probability floor rather than from evidence. Logged for the faithfulness check, never spoken.
